newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia approves $140 million telecoms plan.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia approves $140 million telecoms plan.

text.p: Cambodia took another step towards modernising its creaky telephone system on Thursday with the approval of a $140 million telecommunications master plan, officials said.
Secretary of State So Khun of the Ministry of Posts and Telecommuncations (MPTC) said the planned upgrade, to run until 2009, would help bring Cambodia's often unruly phone system under control.
"It (the plan) has good guidelines to develop telecommunications in the future. We cannot develop telecoms without observing rules and master plans," he told Reuters.
The plan was approved by the cabinet on Thursday.
Ministry officials said it was the first of its kind in Cambodia and would improve transmission and switching networks, tariffs and information systems, as well as human resources.
Cambodia's improving economic growth, following decades of war, has strained its war-ravaged telecommunications structure.
On busy city streets, telephone and electric wiring spill from telegraph poles and it can take dozens of attempts to reach numbers between the three oversubscribed mobile phone networks.

Chris Molloy of Australia's telecommunications group Telstra Corp, which runs the MTPC's international telecommunications, said when his firm arrived in Cambodia in 1990 the country had three overseas circuits -- one to Moscow and two to Vietnam.
"But now communications are improving on a daily basis," he said.
MPTC Undersecretary of State Koy Kim Sea said the master plan would help fix congestion by raising some tariffs, a move expected to improve the balance of traffic between networks.
There have been other promising developments in addition to the master plan, MPTC officials said.
A Japanese cable-laying project will add 10,000 lines by March and 6,000 more by the end of the year.
Separately, Telstra recently implemented direct dialling to the United States and Canada. Global Satellite Mobile (GSM) services are expected to come on line in several weeks.
